#Data Pre-processing:

In this step, we want to:

1. Read the data
```{r}
ev_data <- read.csv("Data/EV_Charging/EV_Charging_Data-_Municipal_Lots_and_Garages_20251106.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
```

2. Choose ID tag as an unique identifier: (still need to consider this decision)
```{r}

# Choose ID_tag as unique identifier
# Check if ID_tag is unique
sum(duplicated(ev_data$`ID Tag`))
# Keep only the first row per ID_tag
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  distinct(`ID Tag`, .keep_all = TRUE)

```

3. Remove Columns and rows that are not relevant to our experiment:
```{r}
# Remove columns: Driver_id, Invalidity_reason, country
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  select(-`Driver ID`, -`Invalidity Reason`, -`Country`)

# Remove rows where session_status is “Disconnected”
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  filter(`Session Status` != "DISCONNECTED")

# Keep Station_name and drop Charger_id
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  select(-`Charge Box ID`)

# Check null values and drop rows with any NA
colSums(is.na(ev_data))
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  tidyr::drop_na()
```

4.Convert type from chr to numeric
```{r}
#change Charge Duration (min) to numeric
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(`Charge Duration (min)` = as.numeric(gsub(",", "", `Charge Duration (min)`)))
#change Connected Duration (min) to numeric
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(`Connected Duration (min)` = as.numeric(gsub(",", "", `Connected Duration (min)`)))
```

5. Add columns based on Dates
```{r}

# Sort the data based on date
ev_data$Date <- as.Date(ev_data$Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  arrange(Date)

# Add weekday column
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(weekday = weekdays(Date))

# Add is_weekend
weekends <- c("Saturday", "Sunday")
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(
    is_weekend = weekday %in% weekends
  )

# Add holidays column for year 2024
# Need to work on this!!
holidays_2024 <- as.Date(c(
  "2024-01-01", # New Year's Day
  "2024-01-15", # MLK Day
  "2024-02-19", # Presidents' Day
  "2024-05-27", # Memorial Day
  "2024-06-19", # Juneteenth
  "2024-07-04", # Independence Day
  "2024-09-02", # Labor Day
  "2024-10-14", # Columbus/Indigenous Peoples' Day
  "2024-11-11", # Veterans Day
  "2024-11-28", # Thanksgiving
  "2024-12-25"  # Christmas
))

ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(
    is_holiday_2024 = Date %in% holidays_2024
  )


```


6. Clean the location names:

```{r}

# Standardize location names
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(
    `Location Name` = case_when(
      # Jerome Gun Hill Road variations
      grepl("JGU|Jerome.*Gun Hill", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Jerome Gun Hill Road Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Bay Ridge variations
      grepl("BRI|Bay Ridge", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Bay Ridge Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Delancey and Essex variations
      grepl("DES|Delancey.*Essex", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Delancey and Essex Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Queens Borough Hall variations
      grepl("QBO|Queensboro Hall|Queens Borough Hall", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Queens Borough Hall Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Jerome 190th Street variations
      grepl("JON|Jerome.*190", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Jerome 190th Street Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # St. George Courthouse variations
      grepl("SGE|St\\.? George", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "St. George Courthouse Garage",
      
      # Court Square variations
      grepl("CSQ|Court Square", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Court Square Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Queens Family Court variations
      grepl("QFA|Queens Family Court", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Queens Family Court Municipal Garage",
      
      # Handle N/A
      `Location Name` == "N/A" ~ NA_character_,
      
      # Keep everything else as is
      TRUE ~ `Location Name`
    )
  )

# Check the results
unique(ev_data$`Location Name`)

# Count how many of each location
ev_data %>% count(`Location Name`, sort = TRUE)

```

7.Add EV charging box brand (manufacturer) as column:

```{r}
# Add Manufacturer column based on Station Name patterns
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(
    Manufacturer = case_when(
      # BTCE followed by four digits - BTC Power
      grepl("^BTCE\\d{4}", `Station Name`) ~ "BTC Power",
      
      # EVB followed by four digits - EVB
      grepl("^EVB\\d{4}", `Station Name`) ~ "EVB",
      
      # EVX1420 or EVX1420z - EVX
      grepl("^EVX1420", `Station Name`) ~ "EVX",
      
      # EV followed by four digits (but not EVB or EVX) - Fast Charger
      grepl("^EV\\d{4}", `Station Name`) ~ "Fast Charger (Multiple)",
      
      # Six digit numbers - Unknown
      grepl("^\\d{6}$", `Station Name`) ~ "Unknown",
      
      # DELETED - Deleted
      grepl("DELETED", `Station Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Deleted",
      
      # Anything else
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )



```

```{r}
### Center and Dispersion Statistics

# Function to calculate mode (R doesn't have a built-in mode function)
get_mode <- function(x) {
  x <- na.omit(x)
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

# Function to calculate all statistics for a variable
calc_stats <- function(x, var_name) {
  x <- na.omit(x)
  
  data.frame(
    Variable = var_name,
    Mean = round(mean(x), 3),
    Median = round(median(x), 3),
    Mode = round(get_mode(x), 3),
    Trimmed_Mean_10pct = round(mean(x, trim = 0.10), 3),
    IQR = round(IQR(x), 3),
    Variance = round(var(x), 3),
    Std_Dev = round(sd(x), 3),
    CV = round((sd(x) / mean(x)) * 100, 2),  # Coefficient of Variation as percentage
    Skewness = round(skewness(x), 3)
  )
}

# Calculate statistics for Energy Provided and Charge Duration
energy_stats <- calc_stats(ev_data$`Energy Provided (kWh)`, "Energy Provided (kWh)")
duration_stats <- calc_stats(ev_data$`Charge Duration (min)`, "Charge Duration (min)")

# Combine into one table
summary_stats <- rbind(energy_stats, duration_stats)

# Display the table
kable(summary_stats, 
      caption = "Summary Statistics: Measures of Center and Dispersion",
      col.names = c("Variable", "Mean", "Median", "Mode", "Trimmed Mean (10%)", 
                    "IQR", "Variance", "Std Dev", "CV (%)", "Skewness"),
      align = "lrrrrrrrrr") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE,
                position = "center")
```

```{r}
### Heatmap of Temporal Usage (Weekday × Hour of Day)

# Prepare data: extract hour and summarize
temporal_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(
    time_object = hms(`Connected Time`),
    hour = hour(time_object)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(hour)) %>%
  group_by(weekday, hour) %>%
  summarise(
    num_sessions = n(),
    avg_energy = round(mean(`Energy Provided (kWh)`, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    total_energy = round(sum(`Energy Provided (kWh)`, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Ensure proper weekday order
temporal_data$weekday <- factor(temporal_data$weekday,
                                 levels = c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday",
                                            "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"))

# 1. Heatmap: Number of Sessions by Weekday × Hour
ggplot(temporal_data, aes(x = hour, y = weekday, fill = num_sessions)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = num_sessions), size = 2.5, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightyellow", high = "darkred") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  labs(title = "Number of Charging Sessions by Day and Hour",
       subtitle = "Identifying peak charging times",
       x = "Hour of Day (24h)",
       y = "Day of Week",
       fill = "Sessions") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

# 2. Heatmap: Average Energy per Session by Weekday × Hour
ggplot(temporal_data, aes(x = hour, y = weekday, fill = avg_energy)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = avg_energy), size = 2.5, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightblue", high = "darkblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  labs(title = "Average Energy per Session by Day and Hour",
       subtitle = "When do longer/fuller charges happen?",
       x = "Hour of Day (24h)",
       y = "Day of Week",

# 3. Heatmap: Total Energy by Weekday × Hour
ggplot(temporal_data, aes(x = hour, y = weekday, fill = total_energy)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightgreen", high = "darkgreen") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  labs(title = "Total Energy Consumed by Day and Hour",
       subtitle = "Grid demand patterns",
       x = "Hour of Day (24h)",

```


#Inferencial Statistics:

### Weekend vs weekday differences


- Two-sample t-tests (or Wilcoxon based on normality) on Charge Duration and Energy Provided:
- 95% CI for the difference in means.
- Have to check for normality (or lack of it) using the histograms + Q–Q plots from desc stats.

```{r}
### Weekend vs Weekday Differences

alpha <- 0.05

# Separate data into weekend and weekday groups
weekday_data <- ev_data %>% filter(is_weekend == FALSE)
weekend_data <- ev_data %>% filter(is_weekend == TRUE)

# Display sample sizes
cat("Sample Sizes:\n")
cat("Weekday sessions:", nrow(weekday_data), "\n")
cat("Weekend sessions:", nrow(weekend_data), "\n")
cat("Significance Level: α =", alpha, "\n")

#-----------------------------------------
# 1. Normality Check: Histograms
#-----------------------------------------

# Histogram: Energy Provided by Weekend vs Weekday
ggplot(ev_data, aes(x = `Energy Provided (kWh)`, fill = is_weekend)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ ifelse(is_weekend, "Weekend", "Weekday"), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Energy Provided: Weekday vs Weekend",
       x = "Energy Provided (kWh)",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("steelblue", "coral"))

# Histogram: Charge Duration by Weekend vs Weekday
ggplot(ev_data, aes(x = `Charge Duration (min)`, fill = is_weekend)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ ifelse(is_weekend, "Weekend", "Weekday"), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Charge Duration: Weekday vs Weekend",
       x = "Charge Duration (min)",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("steelblue", "coral"))

#-----------------------------------------
# 2. Normality Check: Q-Q Plots
#-----------------------------------------

# Q-Q Plot: Energy Provided - Weekday
qqPlot(weekday_data$`Energy Provided (kWh)`,
       main = "Q-Q Plot: Energy Provided (Weekday)",
       ylab = "Energy Provided (kWh)")

# Q-Q Plot: Energy Provided - Weekend
qqPlot(weekend_data$`Energy Provided (kWh)`,
       main = "Q-Q Plot: Energy Provided (Weekend)",
       ylab = "Energy Provided (kWh)")

# Q-Q Plot: Charge Duration - Weekday
qqPlot(weekday_data$`Charge Duration (min)`,
       main = "Q-Q Plot: Charge Duration (Weekday)",
       ylab = "Charge Duration (min)")

# Q-Q Plot: Charge Duration - Weekend
qqPlot(weekend_data$`Charge Duration (min)`,
       main = "Q-Q Plot: Charge Duration (Weekend)",
       ylab = "Charge Duration (min)")


#-----------------------------------------
# 4. Hypothesis Tests for Energy Provided
#-----------------------------------------

# Wilcoxon rank-sum test
wilcox_energy <- wilcox.test(`Energy Provided (kWh)` ~ is_weekend, data = ev_data,
                              conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 1 - alpha)
cat("\n--- Wilcoxon Rank-Sum Test (Non-parametric) ---\n")
cat("W statistic:", wilcox_energy$statistic, "\n")
cat("p-value:", format(wilcox_energy$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
cat("95% CI for difference:", round(wilcox_energy$conf.int[1], 3), "to",
    round(wilcox_energy$conf.int[2], 3), "kWh\n")
cat("Decision:", ifelse(wilcox_energy$p.value < alpha,
                        "Reject H0 - Significant difference exists",
                        "Fail to reject H0 - No significant difference"), "\n")

#-----------------------------------------
# 5. Hypothesis Tests for Charge Duration
#-----------------------------------------

# Wilcoxon rank-sum test
wilcox_duration <- wilcox.test(`Charge Duration (min)` ~ is_weekend, data = ev_data,
                                conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 1 - alpha)
cat("\n--- Wilcoxon Rank-Sum Test (Non-parametric) ---\n")
cat("W statistic:", wilcox_duration$statistic, "\n")
cat("p-value:", format(wilcox_duration$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
cat("95% CI for difference:", round(wilcox_duration$conf.int[1], 3), "to",
    round(wilcox_duration$conf.int[2], 3), "min\n")
cat("Decision:", ifelse(wilcox_duration$p.value < alpha,
                        "Reject H0 - Significant difference exists",
                        "Fail to reject H0 - No significant difference"), "\n")

```


### Location differences


One-way ANOVA on Energy Provided across, let's say, the top 5 Location Name categories in the frequency table.


If ANOVA assumptions fail (from Q–Q plots, boxplots), do Kruskal–Wallis instead.


Chi-square test of independence between Location Name and Energy Provided using the contingency table.


```{r}
### Location Differences Analysis
### Significance Level: α = 0.05

alpha <- 0.05

#-----------------------------------------
# 1. Select Top 5 Locations by Frequency
#-----------------------------------------

top_locations <- ev_data %>%
  count(`Location Name`, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  pull(`Location Name`)

cat("Top 5 Locations by Number of Sessions:\n")
ev_data %>%
  count(`Location Name`, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  print()

# Filter data to top 4 locations
ev_top_locations <- ev_data %>%
  filter(`Location Name` %in% top_locations)

cat("\nFiltered dataset size:", nrow(ev_top_locations), "sessions\n")

#-----------------------------------------
# 2. Descriptive Statistics by Location
#-----------------------------------------

location_summary <- ev_top_locations %>%
  group_by(`Location Name`) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Mean = round(mean(`Energy Provided (kWh)`, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Median = round(median(`Energy Provided (kWh)`, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD = round(sd(`Energy Provided (kWh)`, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Variance = round(var(`Energy Provided (kWh)`, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(location_summary,
      caption = "Energy Provided (kWh) by Location - Descriptive Statistics",
      col.names = c("Location", "n", "Mean", "Median", "Std Dev", "Variance"),
      align = "lrrrrr") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE,
                position = "center")

#-----------------------------------------
# 3. ANOVA Assumption Checks
#-----------------------------------------


# Boxplots - Visual check for outliers and distribution
ggplot(ev_top_locations, aes(x = `Location Name`, y = `Energy Provided (kWh)`,
                              fill = `Location Name`)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "Energy Provided by Location (Top 4)",
       subtitle = "Visual check for ANOVA assumptions",
       x = "Location",
       y = "Energy Provided (kWh)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")

# Q-Q Plots for each location
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
for (loc in top_locations) {
  loc_data <- ev_top_locations %>%
    filter(`Location Name` == loc) %>%
    pull(`Energy Provided (kWh)`)

  qqnorm(loc_data, main = paste("Q-Q Plot:", substr(loc, 1, 25)))
  qqline(loc_data, col = "red", lwd = 2)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Anova doesn't met

#-----------------------------------------
# 4. Kruskal-Wallis Test (Non-parametric alternative)
#-----------------------------------------

cat("\n===== KRUSKAL-WALLIS TEST (Non-parametric) =====\n")
cat("H0: All location distributions are equal\n")
cat("Ha: At least one distribution is different\n")
cat("α =", alpha, "\n\n")

kruskal_result <- kruskal.test(`Energy Provided (kWh)` ~ `Location Name`, data = ev_top_locations)

cat("Chi-squared statistic:", round(kruskal_result$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom:", kruskal_result$parameter, "\n")
cat("p-value:", format(kruskal_result$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Decision:", ifelse(kruskal_result$p.value < alpha,
                        "Reject H0 - Significant difference exists between locations",
                        "Fail to reject H0 - No significant difference"), "\n")

# Post-hoc Dunn Test (if Kruskal-Wallis is significant)
if (kruskal_result$p.value < alpha) {
  cat("\n--- Dunn's Post-Hoc Test (Bonferroni adjustment) ---\n")
  # Need to install FSA package for dunnTest
  if (!require(FSA)) install.packages("FSA", quiet = TRUE)
  library(FSA)
  dunn_result <- dunnTest(`Energy Provided (kWh)` ~ `Location Name`,
                           data = ev_top_locations, method = "bonferroni")
  print(dunn_result)
}

#-----------------------------------------
# 6. Chi-Square Test of Independence
#-----------------------------------------

cat("\n===== CHI-SQUARE TEST OF INDEPENDENCE =====\n")
cat("H0: Location and Energy Category are independent\n")
cat("Ha: Location and Energy Category are dependent\n")
cat("α =", alpha, "\n\n")

# Create energy categories for contingency table
ev_top_locations <- ev_top_locations %>%
  mutate(
    Energy_Category = cut(`Energy Provided (kWh)`,
                          breaks = c(-Inf, 10, 25, 50, Inf),
                          labels = c("Low (0-10)", "Medium (10-25)",
                                     "High (25-50)", "Very High (50+)"))
  )

# Create contingency table
contingency_table <- table(ev_top_locations$`Location Name`,
                           ev_top_locations$Energy_Category)

cat("Contingency Table:\n")
print(contingency_table)

# Visualize contingency table
contingency_df <- as.data.frame(contingency_table)
names(contingency_df) <- c("Location", "Energy_Category", "Count")

ggplot(contingency_df, aes(x = Energy_Category, y = Location, fill = Count)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightyellow", high = "darkred") +
  labs(title = "Contingency Table: Location vs Energy Category",
       x = "Energy Category",
       y = "Location") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Chi-square test
chi_sq_result <- chisq.test(contingency_table)

cat("\n--- Chi-Square Test Results ---\n")
cat("Chi-squared statistic:", round(chi_sq_result$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom:", chi_sq_result$parameter, "\n")
cat("p-value:", format(chi_sq_result$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Decision:", ifelse(chi_sq_result$p.value < alpha,
                        "Reject H0 - Location and Energy Category are DEPENDENT",
                        "Fail to reject H0 - Location and Energy Category are independent"), "\n")

# Expected frequencies (check assumption: all expected counts > 5)
cat("\nExpected Frequencies:\n")
print(round(chi_sq_result$expected, 2))

cat("\nAssumption Check: All expected frequencies > 5?\n")
cat(ifelse(all(chi_sq_result$expected >= 5), "Yes - Assumption met",
           "No - Consider Fisher's exact test or combine categories"), "\n")

#-----------------------------------------
# 7. Summary Table
#-----------------------------------------

summary_tests <- data.frame(
  Test = c("Kruskal-Wallis", "Chi-Square Independence"),
  Statistic = c(paste("χ² =", round(kruskal_result$statistic, 3)),
                paste("χ² =", round(chi_sq_result$statistic, 3))),
  df = c(kruskal_result$parameter,
         chi_sq_result$parameter),
  p_value = c(format(kruskal_result$p.value, scientific = TRUE),
              format(chi_sq_result$p.value, scientific = TRUE)),
  Decision = c(ifelse(kruskal_result$p.value < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0"),
               ifelse(chi_sq_result$p.value < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0"))
)

```


### Proportion inference


One-sample proportion CI and test for weekend sessions:
H0: weekend = 0.3 or some reference value.
Two-sample proportion test: compare weekend usage between two specific locations.


```{r}
### Proportion Inference
### Significance Level: α = 0.05

alpha <- 0.05

#-----------------------------------------
# 1. One-Sample Proportion: Weekend Sessions
#-----------------------------------------

cat("===== ONE-SAMPLE PROPORTION TEST: Weekend Sessions =====\n")
cat("H0: p_weekend = 0.25 (25% of sessions are on weekends)\n")
cat("Ha: p_weekend ≠ 0.25\n")
cat("α =", alpha, "\n\n")

# Calculate observed proportion
n_total <- nrow(ev_data)
n_weekend <- sum(ev_data$is_weekend == TRUE)
p_observed <- n_weekend / n_total

cat("--- Sample Statistics ---\n")
cat("Total sessions:", n_total, "\n")
cat("Weekend sessions:", n_weekend, "\n")
cat("Observed proportion (p̂):", round(p_observed, 4), "\n")
cat("Expected proportion (p0): 0.25\n\n")

# One-sample proportion test
p0 <- 0.25  # Hypothesized proportion
prop_test_one <- prop.test(n_weekend, n_total, p = p0, 
                            conf.level = 1 - alpha, 
                            correct = FALSE)  # Without Yates continuity correction

cat("--- One-Sample z-Test for Proportion ---\n")
cat("Chi-squared statistic:", round(prop_test_one$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format(prop_test_one$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval for p_weekend:", 
    round(prop_test_one$conf.int[1], 4), "to", round(prop_test_one$conf.int[2], 4), "\n")
cat("Decision:", ifelse(prop_test_one$p.value < alpha, 
                        "Reject H0 - Weekend proportion differs from 0.25", 
                        "Fail to reject H0 - No evidence weekend proportion differs from 0.25"), "\n")

# Manual z-test calculation for clarity
z_stat <- (p_observed - p0) / sqrt(p0 * (1 - p0) / n_total)
p_value_z <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z_stat))  # Two-tailed

cat("\n--- Manual z-Test Calculation ---\n")
cat("z-statistic:", round(z_stat, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value (two-tailed):", format(p_value_z, scientific = TRUE), "\n")

# Wilson confidence interval (more accurate for proportions)
cat("\n--- Wilson 95% Confidence Interval ---\n")
wilson_ci <- prop.test(n_weekend, n_total, conf.level = 1 - alpha, correct = FALSE)$conf.int
cat("95% CI:", round(wilson_ci[1], 4), "to", round(wilson_ci[2], 4), "\n")

#-----------------------------------------
# 2. Two-Sample Proportion: Weekend Usage by Location
#-----------------------------------------

cat("\n\n===== TWO-SAMPLE PROPORTION TEST: Weekend Usage by Location =====\n")

# Select two locations for comparison (top 2 by frequency)
top_2_locations <- ev_data %>%
  count(`Location Name`, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(2) %>%
  pull(`Location Name`)

cat("Comparing locations:\n")
cat("  Location 1:", top_2_locations[1], "\n")
cat("  Location 2:", top_2_locations[2], "\n\n")

# Filter data for these two locations
loc1_data <- ev_data %>% filter(`Location Name` == top_2_locations[1])
loc2_data <- ev_data %>% filter(`Location Name` == top_2_locations[2])

# Calculate proportions
n1 <- nrow(loc1_data)
n2 <- nrow(loc2_data)
x1 <- sum(loc1_data$is_weekend == TRUE)
x2 <- sum(loc2_data$is_weekend == TRUE)
p1 <- x1 / n1
p2 <- x2 / n2

cat("--- Sample Statistics ---\n")
cat("Location 1 -", top_2_locations[1], ":\n")
cat("  Total sessions:", n1, "\n")
cat("  Weekend sessions:", x1, "\n")
cat("  Proportion weekend (p̂1):", round(p1, 4), "\n\n")

cat("Location 2 -", top_2_locations[2], ":\n")
cat("  Total sessions:", n2, "\n")
cat("  Weekend sessions:", x2, "\n")
cat("  Proportion weekend (p̂2):", round(p2, 4), "\n\n")

cat("Difference (p̂1 - p̂2):", round(p1 - p2, 4), "\n\n")

# Hypothesis test
cat("H0: p1 = p2 (Weekend proportion is equal at both locations)\n")
cat("Ha: p1 ≠ p2 (Weekend proportions differ)\n")
cat("α =", alpha, "\n\n")

# Two-sample proportion test
prop_test_two <- prop.test(c(x1, x2), c(n1, n2),
                            conf.level = 1 - alpha,
                            correct = FALSE)

cat("--- Two-Sample z-Test for Proportions ---\n")
cat("Chi-squared statistic:", round(prop_test_two$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format(prop_test_two$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
cat("95% CI for difference (p1 - p2):",
    round(prop_test_two$conf.int[1], 4), "to", round(prop_test_two$conf.int[2], 4), "\n")
cat("Decision:", ifelse(prop_test_two$p.value < alpha,
                        "Reject H0 - Weekend proportions differ between locations",
                        "Fail to reject H0 - No significant difference in weekend proportions"), "\n")

# Manual z-test calculation
p_pooled <- (x1 + x2) / (n1 + n2)
se_pooled <- sqrt(p_pooled * (1 - p_pooled) * (1/n1 + 1/n2))
z_stat_two <- (p1 - p2) / se_pooled
p_value_z_two <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z_stat_two))

cat("\n--- Manual z-Test Calculation ---\n")
cat("Pooled proportion:", round(p_pooled, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard error:", round(se_pooled, 4), "\n")
cat("z-statistic:", round(z_stat_two, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value (two-tailed):", format(p_value_z_two, scientific = TRUE), "\n")

#-----------------------------------------
# 3. Visualization
#-----------------------------------------

# Bar plot comparing weekend proportions by location
prop_comparison <- data.frame(
  Location = c(top_2_locations[1], top_2_locations[2]),
  Weekend_Proportion = c(p1, p2),
  Weekend_Count = c(x1, x2),
  Total_Count = c(n1, n2)
)

ggplot(prop_comparison, aes(x = Location, y = Weekend_Proportion, fill = Location)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Weekend_Proportion * 100, 1), "%\n(",
                                Weekend_Count, "/", Total_Count, ")")),
            vjust = -0.3, size = 4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.25, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 0.32, label = "Reference: 25%", color = "red") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 0.5),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Weekend Session Proportion by Location",
       subtitle = paste("Two-sample test p-value:", format(prop_test_two$p.value, scientific = TRUE)),
       x = "Location",
       y = "Proportion of Weekend Sessions") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")

# #-----------------------------------------
# # 4. Summary Table
# #-----------------------------------------
# 
# summary_proportion <- data.frame(
#   Test = c("One-Sample (Weekend = 0.30)", 
#            paste("Two-Sample (", substr(top_2_locations[1], 1, 15), " vs ", 
#                  substr(top_2_locations[2], 1, 15), ")", sep = "")),

#                paste0(round(p1 * 100, 2), "% vs ", round(p2 * 100, 2), "%")),

#                      paste("χ² =", round(prop_test_two$statistic, 3))),

#               format(prop_test_two$p.value, scientific = TRUE)),

#                    round(prop_test_one$conf.int[2], 4), ")"),

#                ifelse(prop_test_two$p.value < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0"))
# )
```
